A particle's light read once per block position per frame (with the particle records).
Particles' block-shape questions answered once per tick and block instead of once per particle (with parallel particles).

exp/render-priority (client): the render thread (and the singleplayer server's) above the game's other threads, so a frame does not wait for its core behind background work - on a 4-core PC (Intel N100) stutters 7.9 -> 1.3 %, the slowest frames 50 -> 21 ms.

Sounds start without waiting for the sound thread to hand out a channel (a mod that works there - Sound Physics Remastered - held every frame up next to a crowd of mobs); when that thread is far behind a new sound is dropped, as the game drops one when no channel is free.

GPU terrain: chunk sections meshed on the graphics card from the blocks as the server sends them, far terrain as coarser cells (level of detail beyond 6 chunks, coarser again beyond 10). Less CPU per frame and fewer triangles: on an Intel N100 a flight 88 -> 166 fps. Near terrain looks the same; far terrain is simplified. Blocks whose look mods compute from the world are drawn the vanilla way. Stands aside (vanilla terrain) when another mod replaces the chunk renderer: Sodium, Embeddium and the shader mods on them.
GPU terrain: level of detail closer (from 4 chunks, coarser from 8) - for weak graphics; the middle distance looks coarser.
GPU terrain: terrain toward the screen edges and behind goes coarse sooner. A few more fps; after a fast turn detail fills in over a moment.

Up to a few seconds at start in large packs.
